newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong silent on Korean defections.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong silent on Korean defections.

text.p: Hong Kong authorities on Thursday declined to comment on reports that 17 North Koreans fled to the British colony via China and were seeking asylum in South Korea.
"It remains the government's policy not to comment on individual cases," a government spokesman said in reply to questions about news reports from Seoul.
Earlier, a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman said the 17 had entered China on October 26 and crossed on November 23 into Hong Kong, where they were being held in a refugee centre.
Hong Kong's immigration department, border police, Security Branch and governor's office, along with the South Korean consulate in Hong Kong, all witheld comment.

The Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said it was the biggest ever mass defection from the communist North. The group was helped by ethnic Koreans living in China who were paid to act as guides by relatives of the escapees in the United States.
All but one of the group, which included five children and a pregnant woman, were relatives. The other defector is a North Korean security official, the Seoul spokesman said.
The previous largest defection to South Korea from North Korea was in 1987 when doctor Kim Man-chol, his wife and nine relatives came to the South via a third country.
